entries.subject: ESA/Hubble potw1208a
entries.finding: Preview of a forthcoming supernova: ACS at 220, 250, 330, 550 and 660 nm; 1089 × 1033 px over 27.0 × 25.6 arcsec, released 20 February 2012. The file's embedded sky tags for scale and direction, 0.0248 arcsec per pixel and north 34.98° left of vertical, and the star for place: the middle of the picture's saturated pixels, pixel 627, 525, is set at Eta Carinae's catalogued place, so the frame's centre is 161.2656327°, -59.684052°.

entries.subject: The nebula's surface
entries.finding: Steffen et al. (2014) mapped the whole Homunculus with VLT/X-shooter in H2 2.12 µm and made the first full 3D model of it: a single continuous surface for each lobe, with the polar holes, trenches and near-equatorial protrusions the spectra show. The optical picture is light the star scatters off the dust of that thin, clumpy shell. NASA publishes the model as a file for printing; the bake reads where each sight line crosses it.

entries.subject: How the model lies on the picture
entries.finding: Smith (2006) prints the pole: an inclination of 41.0 ± 0.5 degrees, the tilt of the polar axis out of the line of sight, along position angle 310 degrees. The file prints nothing of its unit, its turn about the pole, the star's place or which end recedes. Measured here (packages/bake/authoring/homunculus-nebula/model-fit.mts): the +z end recedes, the turn is 328 degrees, a unit is 2.72 arcsec and the star is at (0.96, 0, -0.08) of the file; the model's outline then shares 86.8% with the picture's lit pixels. A check against a printed number: the file's farthest point along its pole is 3.89 units from the star, 10.6 arcsec, 3.72e15 m at 2,350 pc, beside the 3.4e15 m at which Steffen et al. state the lobes' speeds.

entries.subject: The sides the picture does not show
entries.finding: One picture shows the side of each lobe that faces the Sun. The far sides, and the part of the north-west lobe behind the south-east one, have not been photographed. Each lobe is unwrapped on a Mercator chart about the sight line and its unseen cells filled block by block from the seen ones of both lobes (image quilting, Efros and Freeman 2001), the seams relaxed by Poisson blending: a presentation choice, not what those sides look like.

entries.subject: The equatorial skirt
entries.finding: Steffen et al. (2014) and Smith (2006) find no H2 from the thin equatorial skirt, so the model has no surface for it. Smith (2009) and Davidson et al. (2001) find it thin and planar. Its two fans are regions drawn by hand on the picture (source/regions.json) and laid on five sheets fanning 6 degrees either side of the plane through the star across the pole: a thickness the papers do not measure, so modeled.

entries.subject: Hubble's 2019 ultraviolet picture
entries.finding: ESA/Hubble heic1912a (WFC3, Mg II 280 nm, 336 nm and [N II] 658 nm; 1779 x 1805 px, released 1 July 2019) is not drawn as a picture: the nebula has expanded since the 2012 picture the lobes carry. Its red channel lights the gas cloud's dots in the optical dataset. Its scale, 0.02294 arcsec a pixel, and the star's pixel are fitted against the 2014 Hubble F658N image (correlation 0.68; packages/bake/authoring/homunculus-nebula/outer-ejecta/heic-registration.mts).

entries.subject: Hubble · optical: the picture on the lobes, and the gas cloud around them
entries.finding: The default dataset. The lobes: ESA/Hubble potw1208a on Steffen et al. (2014)'s closed mesh, as the entries above describe. The gas cloud: 7,358 dots (source/cloud-points.json), derived by this repository, neither observed in 3D nor published. Their places are the 762 measured knots within 45 arcsec of the star's sky plane, each depth mirrored to the far side by assumption; their light heic1912a's [N II] red, and beyond its field the 2003 WFPC2 F658N mosaic scaled by 3.42 from the 412 knots both see; 638 are dark dust where the optical picture is darker than the gas around it. The lobes' occluder is two ellipsoids fitted to the mesh. Baked by packages/bake/cli/prepare-cloud-points.mts into 300 billboards of about 25 dots, each drawn once from Earth into a 96 px atlas cell (prepared/cloud.bin, cssearth-cloud-points@1).

entries.subject: Outer shell · model: the 1840s ejecta's outer shell
entries.finding: Mehner et al. (2016, A&A 595, A120) model the 1840s material outside the Homunculus with SHAPE as a bent, partial cylinder; the open parts are not seen in MUSE (their Fig. 4), and SHAPE fits brightness, not density. The model is not released as data, so packages/bake/authoring/homunculus-nebula/outer-ejecta/tube.mts refits that shape to 17,097 MUSE H-beta detections faster than 450 km/s: position angle 322.7 degrees, tilt 26.6 degrees, radius 11.5 to 16.7 arcsec; 68% of the detections within 3 arcsec of the wall (source/tube.json). Drawn as 744 wireframe segments (prepared/outer-shell.bin); the 216 within 3 arcsec of a detection solid, the rest faint. Labeled a model.

entries.subject: Motions · measured: the outer ejecta's knots and where they move
entries.finding: 891 knots (source/kinematics.json): 2.4 arcsec tiles of the 2014 F658N image tracked through eleven Hubble epochs, 1993 to 2020, by normalized cross-correlation after Kiminki et al. (2016), with a MUSE H-beta line-of-sight speed each and a depth of rho v_los / v_tan, which assumes motion straight out from the star. 764 knots within 60 arcsec of the sky plane are drawn as arrows of their motion over 100 years at 2.3 kpc, blue approaching and red receding (prepared/motions.bin). The others are left out: their line-of-sight speed is too large for their sky motion to be the same material's.

entries.subject: The outer ejecta's chain, run from the archives
entries.finding: outer-ejecta.mts, run from the archive downloads on 2026-10-11, wrote the three shipped source records: 891 knots, the tube and 7,358 dots; rebaking them reproduces every prepared file byte for byte. Sky motions are matched in double precision: in masked areas, which are zero, single-precision rounding can make a false match (one tile in 2020 at correlation 0.925 across a 49 px jump, where the true best is 0.496).

entries.subject: Motions within one instrument
entries.finding: The tracker matches every epoch, WFPC2, ACS and WFC3, against the 2014 ACS image. Kiminki et al. (2016, Sect. 2.2) measure only WFPC2 to WFPC2 and ACS to ACS: WFPC2's F658N passes [N II] from -615 to +1,130 km/s, ACS's up to +-1,600 km/s with much H-alpha, so a knot's shape can differ between them. Matching also reads masked pixels as zero rather than ignoring them, and reflection ghosts have no mask of their own.
entries.revisitWhen: Motions measured within each instrument, with mask-aware matching, are compared with these.

entries.subject: Dating each knot by rho / mu
entries.finding: An ejection year of rho / mu, with no slowing down, is unreliable here: in source/kinematics.json 645 of 891 knots date before 1780 and 71 before the year 0. No date is shown. The tube fit still drops detections near tiles dated before 1780, so it rests on these dates.
entries.revisitWhen: Dates are measured with deceleration or taken from Kiminki et al.'s within-instrument catalogue.

entries.subject: Mehner et al.'s SHAPE model as data
entries.finding: The paper's SHAPE model is not released as data, so the shape is refitted here. The refit's tilt, 26.6 degrees, lies near its 25 degree lower bound, so the bound may set it.
entries.revisitWhen: The authors release the SHAPE model, or the refit is rerun with a wider tilt range and compared.

entries.subject: Every dot redrawn each frame as an SVG sprite
entries.finding: On an iPad (9th generation) a frame took about 131 to 170 ms, and the page was blocked while the camera moved.
entries.revisitWhen: A browser redraws thousands of SVG sprites a frame within the frame budget on the iPad.

entries.subject: One 2D affine warp of the whole dot layer while the camera moves
entries.finding: 27 to 42 frames a second on the iPad, but visibly wrong: a single warp cannot show parallax about the orbit target, and the layer jumped when the camera settled.
entries.revisitWhen: Only for a layer without depth; one warp cannot draw parallax.

entries.subject: Five depth slabs, each warped
entries.finding: 31 to 49 frames a second on the iPad; the nearest slab streaked.
entries.revisitWhen: The billboards prove too slow on a target device.

entries.subject: Dots as 3D sprites in the lobes' CSS scene
entries.finding: About 12 times slower than the billboards on the desktop.
entries.revisitWhen: Browsers composite thousands of 3D-transformed elements cheaply.

entries.subject: The tube textured with the photo or F658N; nested tubes; a cocoon
entries.finding: The tube textured with the photo or the F658N image showed seams and wrong colors. Nested tubes and a cocoon around the lobes were tried and not kept. The wireframe shows only the fitted shape, and which parts MUSE sees.
entries.revisitWhen: A measured emission map on the shell exists.

entries.subject: Envelope shells as a red filtering medium in front of the lobes
entries.finding: Meant to explain the lobes' color difference. Each shell applied one transmission to all three channels and added red light: grey attenuation plus emission, not wavelength-dependent extinction, and it counted shell crossings rather than path length. An independent review (Codex) also found that the papers attribute the lobes' reddening to dust in their walls and scattering geometry, and that faint surrounding emission does not measure dust optical depth.
entries.revisitWhen: A dust scattering and extinction model of the lobes themselves is fitted.

entries.subject: Gas clumps as crossed squares
entries.finding: Clumps of gas drawn on crossed squares were tried and not kept; the billboards, which always face the camera, replaced them.
entries.revisitWhen: Clumps need a shape of their own seen from the side.
